metadata.note: Alabama, Tennessee and Northern (Carrollton Short Line 1897, renamed AT&N RR 1906; consolidated with the Tombigbee Valley and Mobile Terminal & Ry 1 May 1913; reorganised 1918) - Reform to Mobile, 220 mi. One through daily train served the whole line. Frisco bought control in 1948 (merger 1971); passenger service ended in or before 1948, so nothing is drawn in Frisco colour. Drawn: the AT&N in five pieces by first passenger year, its 1924-1928 trackage-rights route into Mobile over the Southern, its own Mobile extension 1928-1948, the Tombigbee Valley 1906/1908-1913, and two 3 ft gauge predecessor anchors (1893, 1902).

segments.note: Carrollton Short Line Railway, built because the M&O bypassed the Pickens County seat; renamed Alabama, Tennessee & Northern Railroad 29 Sep 1906 (a rename of the same corporation, not an ownership change). START 1902: msrailroads says the line opened October 1900, the Carrollton historical marker (hmdb 178594, read only via a search summary) says the first train reached Carrollton in 1902, and the company reported 3 leased passenger cars on 30 Jun 1902. 1902 is drawn as the later end of that conflict and the first year passenger equipment is documented. Reform and Carrollton appear in the 1924 and 1934 company timetables (Fowler 'bc'). The Pickens County marker's 29 Jun 1976 'last train' is a FREIGHT date. END 1948: the only explicit end date is chicagorailfan ('Passenger service discontinued in 1948'), a single uncited secondary source. The last CONFIRMED passenger year is 1942 (same page: No. 2 left Mobile for Reform 8:25 am, No. 1 arrived Mobile 4:45 pm, one daily round trip). 1943-1948 is drawn on the strength of that one source; it conflicts with nothing found, but nothing else confirms it. The Feb 1952 Official Guide daggers AT&N stations as freight-only, so the line must never be drawn past 1948. Frisco bought control in 1948; freight continued under Frisco (merged 1971) and BN. headway_min 1440 = one daily round trip, sourced only for 1942 (chicagorailfan); 1911 'through daily passenger service' (Geiger Times). Other years are an estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: ANOTHER COMPANY'S TRACK: this feature is drawn on the Southern Railway (today Norfolk Southern 3-B South District) Calvert - Chickasaw - Mobile line, which the AT&N used under trackage rights; it is coloured AT&N because these were AT&N trains (Rule 4). segments.note: AT&N trains ran into Mobile Terminal Station over the Southern Railway's Mobile line via Chickasaw, under trackage rights (ICC: 'North Mobile to Calvert, 30.0 miles'), until the AT&N's own Mobile extension opened in 1928. START 1924: the first confirmed year - Fowler's footnote 'until 1928, service operated via SOU Calvert-Chickasaw and to Mobile (Terminal)' is attached to the 1924 timetable; a 1920s photo (UWA) shows an AT&N passenger train at Mobile. The rights may have been used from 1913, but no earlier year is confirmed. Before this, Tombigbee Valley passengers changed to the Southern at Calvert. Headway: one daily round trip is an estimate carried back from 1942.

properties.line: Seaboard Railway of Alabama: Calvert – Tuscarora
properties.speed_source: estimated: 3 ft gauge logging line; no running time sourced. Rule 3.
properties.geometry_source: Geometry is the Riderwood - Calvert AT&N trace (OSM, old_railway_operator=Frisco) cut at the projected chainage of the Nominatim points; same alignment as the AT&N feature. OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py over railtrace degree-tiles plus OSM abandoned/rail-trail ways and OpenHistoricalMap ways for the corridor. The AT&N is tagged old_railway_operator=Frisco in OSM (its 1948-1971 controller), on both the live Alabama & Gulf Coast track and the abandoned grade; no 'AT&N' or 'Alabama, Tennessee and Northern' spelling is in use. Waypoints are Nominatim town/hamlet/census-place points (every type checked; none was a county), plus hand-pinned Mobile terminals.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 19.7 mi against a documented 21-24 mi (Fowler mp 165-186 to Calvert; River Junction adds 3). 3 FT GAUGE ON THE LATER ALIGNMENT: this narrow-gauge predecessor is drawn on the standard-gauge Tombigbee Valley / AT&N alignment (OSM old_railway_operator=Frisco, cut from the Riderwood - Calvert trace). The narrow gauge followed approximately the same corridor, but its exact grade - and its original river terminus at Nannahubba Bluff / River Junction, 3 mi from Calvert, which is not drawn - is not traced; local deviations are likely. No approximated (straight-line) legs.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] 3 ft gauge logging line (Wikipedia: the 'Seaboard Railroad', 33 mi, bought by Cochrane at foreclosure in 1897) from River Junction / Calvert to Tuscarora, later Seaboard (mp 165), via Brownlow, Howards and Chatta (Topton). 1893 is the ONLY proven passenger year - the 1893 Official Guide lists it with Tuscarora as terminus (Fowler 'z', 'z(tm)'). Service certainly ran wider both ways, but no other year is confirmed; do not widen this anchor to look plausible. Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Tombigbee & Northern Railway, 3 ft gauge, Calvert north via Chastang, Seaboard, Van Vlecks Mill and Main Line Junction toward Penny Mill. 1902 is the ONLY proven passenger year - the 1902 Official Guide shows Penny Mill as terminus (Fowler 1902G(tm)). Service certainly ran wider both ways (to the 1904 reorganisation as the Tombigbee Valley), but no other year is confirmed; do not widen it. Drawn Calvert - Chatom only: Penny Mill is unlocated (Hilton says it became Millry, but 1902G puts it 9 mi from Chatom), so the Chatom - Penny Mill stub is omitted. Headway is an estimate.
